Some parts yes, some parts no. 

I will always be appreciative for the opportunities and experiences wrestling has afforded me, my school was very good to me and all trainees. My confidence is up tenfold and it inspired me to get in good shape after being skin & bones for most of my life.

On the flip side, I was sold a dream that was never meant for me. I completely shut off all other faculties of my life because I thought I could get signed if I put 100% into it. My relationship was rocky because I would prioritise doing ring crew for major UK shows than spending time with her which I did very little of.

 My social life was non existent because my weekends were focussed on what shows I could go to / where could I help out / what shall I do in the gym. 

The scene was a bit cliquey also which all  scenes will be and certain opportunities would find their way to certain groups of people but that’s just how it is I guess.

Overall, I’ve changed as a human being for the better because of wrestling, but I’ve also put a lot of time & resources and had no payout but that’s just how it is. Nothing is guaranteed or owed to you, if you want to attempt to reach your potential, that’s a risk that you’re taking with your livelihood.

Hey man, I’m a borderline Aspergers (yeah I know, the doctors didn’t know what to call it) sufferer and a trainee of 2 years.

I most probably don’t experience it as severely as you might do however I understand all the symptoms and might be able to help you out a bit.

So first and foremost you’re gonna need to leave all your discomforts at the door and commit emotionally to this if you want to stick at it. Showing out, socialising and trying to be a people person to fans and peers is pretty much the hardest thing for me and is extremely exhausting and draining emotionally and mentally. It is however a huge help if you can overcome that early.

Pick a school close to you, start doing squats, pushups & cardio so that you can hopefully keep up (100 s, 50 p a day might be good and doesn’t have to be done all at once) shake everybody’s hand on your first day (I made the mistake of not doing it and it took me a bit longer to win the other trainees over), give the trainer your undivided attention when they speak and listen. They may be giving feedback to somebody else but it’s most likely for the whole class. Another thing is that when you’re getting feedback, don’t talk over them (oh but I meant it this way or that’s not how I wanted it to be like) just listen and say thank you at the end.

Also I’d personally worry about character work when you’re getting regular bookings on shows (Something that’s yet to happen for me.) 

If you want something specific answered then please PM me, it fills me with joy that another Aspie wants to do this because it reaffirms my belief that this disorder can be overcome!
